newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia rubber stable in quiet late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia rubber stable in quiet late trade.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 rubber prices were stable in late trading on Tuesday, with gains in Tokyo lifting sentiment, traders said.
But they said Malaysian rubber had a competitive edge because of a slight discount to SIR20 prices following the Malaysian currency's weakening against the U.S. dollar.
"Malaysia's SMR20 is half-a-cent cheaper than SIR20," one trader said. "The discount is putting pressure on us."
Traders said dealers from Singapore, the United States and Europe made enquiries but no deals were done.
They said September SIR20 was done at 40.75 cents/lb fob Pontianak and 43.75 cents fob Surabaya late on Monday, while November SIR20 was done at 44.50 cents fob Medan.
"The higher closing in Tokyo usually helps us," one trader said. "I expect prices to remain steady through the week."
They said September shipment SIR20 offers were quoted unchanged at 43.50-44.00 cents/lb fob Medan, 43.50-43.75 cents fob Padang, Palembang and Surabaya.
